CausalChain: Tumor hypoxia -> stabilization of HIF-1α -> upregulation of DNMT1 -> epigenetic modifications that promote increased IL-6 expression -> binding of IL-6 to its receptor triggering JAK2 activation -> STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation -> transcription of genes driving EMT, cancer stemness and chemoresistance -> sustained hypoxic microenvironment
Hypothesis: In hypoxic tumor environments, HIF-1α-driven upregulation of DNMT1 establishes an epigenetically reinforced feed-forward loop with IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling that sustains cancer stem cell traits and chemoresistance; thus, dual inhibition of hypoxia-induced epigenetic reprogramming and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling may better impair malignant progression.
Abstract: Recent research has underscored the pivotal role of the IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway in modulating tumor growth, metastasis, and drug resistance through its impacts on cancer-associated fibroblasts, inflammation and epithelial‐mesenchymal transition. We propose a novel hypothesis that tumor hypoxia acts in synergy with the IL‐6 axis by triggering epigenetic reprogramming in malignant cells. In particular, hypoxia-induced stabilization of HIF-1α may upregulate DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), leading to modifications that favor sustained IL-6 production and persistent STAT3 activation. This feed-forward loop may enhance cancer stem cell phenotypes and chemoresistance. Intervening in both hypoxia-mediated epigenetic changes and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling might therefore yield synergistic anti-tumor effects.
